The integers from 1 to 64 are placed into an \(8 \times 8\) grid. We want to maximize 
\[
M = \sum_{i=1}^8 \sum_{j=1}^7 \bigl(|a_{i,j+1} - a_{i,j}| + |a_{j+1,i} - a_{j,i}|\bigr),
\]
the sum of absolute differences over all horizontal and vertical adjacent pairs.

The grid graph is bipartite with 32 cells of each color. Any numbering induces an orientation on edges from smaller to larger numbers. If we write \(c_v = (\text{out-degree}) - (\text{in-degree})\) for each vertex, then \(M = \sum_v a_v c_v\). To maximize \(M\), we want the largest coefficients \(c_v\) to pair with the largest numbers. The set of possible coefficient vectors comes from acyclic orientations. The maximum sum of the positive coefficients is bounded by the total number of edges, 112, achieved only when all edges are directed from one color class to the other. This gives exactly 32 positive coefficients equal to the degrees of the cells in that class, and 32 negative coefficients equal to minus the degrees in the other class.

The \(8 \times 8\) grid has:
- 4 corners (degree 2),
- 24 edge cells (degree 3),
- 36 interior cells (degree 4).
Under checkerboard coloring, each color class contains 2 corners (deg 2), 12 edge cells (deg 3), and 18 interior cells (deg 4).

Assign the largest 32 numbers \(\{33,34,\dots,64\}\) to one color class and the smallest 32 numbers \(\{1,2,\dots,32\}\) to the other. Within each class, match the largest numbers to the highest degrees to maximize \(M\):
- Largest class: assign the top 18 numbers to degree 4, the next 12 to degree 3, the last 2 to degree 2.
- Smallest class: assign the bottom 18 numbers to degree 4, the next 12 to degree 3, the largest 2 to degree 2.

Calculate the contributions:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{Large class sum} &= 4\sum_{k=47}^{64} k + 3\sum_{k=35}^{46} k + 2(34+33) \\
&= 4\cdot 999 + 3\cdot 486 + 2\cdot 67 = 3996 + 1458 + 134 = 5588,\\[4pt]
\text{Small class sum} &= 4\sum_{k=1}^{18} k + 3\sum_{k=19}^{30} k + 2(31+32) \\
&= 4\cdot 171 + 3\cdot 294 + 2\cdot 63 = 684 + 882 + 126 = 1692.
\end{aligned}
\]
Then \(M_{\max} = 5588 - 1692 = 3896\).

The remainder when 3896 is divided by 1000 is \(896\).

\boxed{896}
